report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the cooking/culinary/restaurant domain (recipes, baking, kitchen/chef/professional food context).

Reasoning
- Logit-lens tokens repeatedly and dominantly point to culinary vocabulary across many high-norm cells and positions, especially in higher layers (18–25): “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Cooking/cooking,” “Chef,” “kitchen,” “baking/Baked/Bake,” “Cake,” “microwave,” “oven,” “culinary,” “Professional/professional,” “Kitchen,” “Mediterranean,” “Baker.”
- Earlier high-norm layers also show food/food-writing adjectives: “culinary,” “delectable,” “exquisite,” “hottest,” “Restaurant,” alongside related “Innovation”/“metropolitan”/“dissertation” noise, but the dominant, consistent theme is food/recipes/restaurants.
- Difference norms are concentrated in later layers and across positions (esp. pos1–pos4), consistent with a high-level semantic/style shift rather than a low-level tokenization quirk.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B appears more likely to produce or steer toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content and related professional kitchen terminology.
